title: Cyperus rotundus L.: Phytochemistry, Nutritional Potential, Medicinal Properties, and Emerging Application
content: Cyperus rotundus L. (purple nutsedge) is an invasive plant whose tubers and rhizomes contain nutrients and diverse phytochemicals with potential nutritional and pharmacological relevance. This narrative review critically integrates evidence on its nutritional composition, redox-active constituents, molecular mechanisms, biological activities, and emerging applications, highlight-ing the relationships between oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, and metabolic regulation. The plant contains resistant starch, dietary fiber, minerals, phenolic compounds, flavonoids, ter-penoids, phytosterols, and essential-oil constituents. Experimental studies suggest that selected extracts and isolated compounds exhibit antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, with re-ported or proposed involvement of Nrf2/HO-1, NF-κB, MAPK, mitochondrial, and metabolic pathways. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for interpreting the pharmacological potential of C. rotundus and investigating its applications in functional foods, nutraceuticals, and other formulations. However, the evidence remains predominantly preclinical, with substantial variability in plant materials and extraction procedures, limited pharmacokinetic and bioavaila-bility data, and insufficient long-term safety and clinical evidence. The main contribution of this review is to distinguish experimentally supported findings from proposed mechanisms while identifying the major barriers to translation. Standardized preparations, mechanistic validation, exposure assessment, and well-designed clinical trials are essential before the therapeutic or in-dustrial potential of C. rotundus can be established.
